facts.fact: UNICEF Lesotho says birth registration stations in health facilities are supported by a low-tech SMS-based platform for registering births; deaths are not mentioned (no event date given; the post's date is used).

UNICEF Lesotho says 30 birth registration stations have been established in government and CHAL health facilities across three districts, Maseru, Berea and Leribe, supported by an SMS-based platform; no total of offices is given (no event date given; the post's date is used).

UNICEF Lesotho says the Government of Lesotho set up the 30 SMS-supported birth registration stations with support from the Government of Japan and UNICEF; no domestic budget is mentioned (the post's date is used).

UNICEF Lesotho reports that 30 birth registration stations supported by an SMS-based platform have been established in health facilities in Maseru, Berea and Leribe (no date of establishment given; the post's date is used).

systems.owner: Government of Lesotho, with Government of Japan and UNICEF support
systems.tiers: 30 stations in government and CHAL health facilities in Maseru, Berea and Leribe

note: Classed civil because the document calls the health-facility points birth registration stations; it does not say whether the SMS message is itself the registration or a notification to the registrar, nor how the record is held.
